name: Binary accretion
blurb: Two point masses orbiting inside a gas disk: they clear a cavity, draw streams across it and accrete.

featured.label: m₁ (M☉)
featured.tip: Mass of the heavier body, in solar masses. It sets only the physical units the readouts are shown in (with the separation). A barotropic gas runs on unchanged; another equation of state takes physical constants from them, and starts again

featured.label: Separation (pc)
featured.tip: Semi-major axis of the binary’s orbit, in parsecs. It sets only the physical units the readouts are shown in (with m₁). A barotropic gas runs on unchanged; another equation of state takes physical constants from them, and starts again

featured.label: Mass ratio
featured.tip: Mass of the lighter body over the heavier one. Sets the orbit: changing it starts the run again

featured.label: Eccentricity
featured.tip: Eccentricity of the binary’s orbit. Changing it starts the run again

featured.label: Softening and sink radius
featured.tip: Radius within which each mass’s pull is softened and it takes in gas (at least two cells). Changes take effect without a restart

featured.label: Binary inclination (°)
featured.tip: Angle between the binary’s orbit and the disk, in degrees, tilted about the line through pericenter: 0 orbits with the disk, 90 is polar, 180 against it. Changing it starts the run again

featured.label: Retrograde
featured.tip: The binary orbits against the disk’s rotation. Changing it starts the run again
